newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia could be one of the smaller trading countries most affected by a fall in Japan's sharemarket that has cast a shadow over the strength of the world economy for 1997. The Nikkei index has fallen 16 percent over the last five weeks and if the fears over the fall were realised, the world economic recovery could be seriously dented. Page 1.

Bunnings and BBC Hardware, the two giants of Australia's A$15 billion hardware retailing sector, are planning to launch a A$500 million bid for market domination. The aim of the two firms is to centre on a four-year expansion of their megastore strategy and eventually win about half of the 65 percent of hardware sales still controlled by independent stores. Page 1.

While the board of Highlands Gold Ltd will meet today to discuss a final attempt to reach a deal with Placer Dome Inc, Placer's adviser, Macquarie Corporate Finance director Tony Ferguson, said Placer would not enter into any further negotiations or entertain further proposals, following the collapse of Highlands' A$160 million underwriting agreement. Page 17.

A strategic review of non-core assets has resulted in the sale of BHP's Hawaiian gas distribution business Gasco to U.S. utility Citizens Utilities Co for A$128 million. However, the sale is dependent on regulatory approval and may not settle until after BHP's 1996/97 financial year ends on May 31. Page 18.

Reef Casino Trust directors will hold a crisis meeting today, after a banking syndicate led by the ANZ Banking Group last week threatened to impose a 14-day deadline for the casino to rectify breaches of its loan covenants. The syndicate wants to reduce the trust's debt from A$105 million to around A$60 million, but Reef casino operator Casinos Austria International Ltd has rejected suggestions that it should make the entire A$40 million capital injection. Page 18.

According to Rebel Sport Ltd joint managing director Ian Dresner, a full-scale takeover of the rest of the company is likely if one of four potential bidders, including Coles Myer Ltd and Singapore's Ossia International, buys Sam Linz's 38 percent stake in Rebel Sport. However, Dresner did not rule out a management buyout. Page 18.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Local markets will be off to a jittery start when they open this morning following warnings about an overheating United States economy and the threat of inflation. Bond markets in the United States dived on Friday after the release of economic data that showed a jump in payrolls that were significantly above predictions. Page 17.

In its supplementary submission lodged at the weekend, the Australian Securities Commission has asked the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system to consider developing the existing ASC structure wherever possible. The move, considered a push by the ASC for more power, could see it in an expanded role in regulating superannuation, investments and consumer complaints if it were implemented in full. Page 17.

OneTel, a venture into telecommunications by Rodney Adler, James Packer, Jodee Rich and Brad Keeling that has only been up and running for 18 months, has given the owners a small bonanza by paying a maiden dividend of A$1 million. The profit, showed in documents to the Australian Securities Commission, was struck after tax of A$600,000 and followed a loss of A$660,000 the previous year. Page 19.

A case heard in the Perth Federal Court last month over whether offshore drilling company Maretech CMDL Pty Ltd should be subject to fringe benefits tax on a A$31.50 daily living away from home allowance paid to its crew members has been decided on the fine distinction between an oil rig and a mobile drilling ship. The case highlights Australia's unclear local tax laws. Page 19.

Following last week's conditional agreement between Highlands Gold and its takeover predator Canada's Placer Dome Inc, which saw Placer dropping its 75 cents a share takeover offer and being offered to purchase Highland's 25 percent stake in the Porgera mine, Highlands will today hold an urgent board meeting in a last minute bid to secure a A$160 million capital raising needed to fend off Placer. Page 19.

The Securities Institute of Australia said yesterday in its submission to the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system that Australia had to pursue the changing global marketplace and remain cost competitive or risk being left behind by its rivals Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The BBC Hardware chain is surviving well in Australia despite a housing slump and general depressed retail conditions. The driving force behind the success of BBC is deputy managing director ofo Howard Smith, Ian Tsicalas, who says he is happy with the company's performance, but believes it can do better. Page 33.

The Australian sharemarket is expected to reach a record high this week in the wake of a rampaging Wall Street which reached another record high on Friday night. The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit 6,703.79 and the Australian All Ordinaries, which droped 4.6 points to close on Friday at 2,418.6 following a bad trading session in Japan, should follow suit today. Page 33.

There is speculation today over whether Kerry Packer will strike a deal to buy out the United States-based Showboat from its management agreement and shareholding in Sydney Harbour Casino. As word spread about talks between Packer's camp and the Showboat management, shares in the casino rose six cents to A$1.93 on Friday. Page 33.

An Australian Gas Light Company spokesman said yesterday New South Wales is expected to move to an open access gas network system following AGL's amending of its access undertaking, as it is being strongly criticised by its major industrial customers. Neotiations are close to completion, allowing the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal to make a decision on the access code that would be in the best interests of all parties. Page 33.

The Securities Institute of Australia said yesterday in its submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system that Australia must embrace the global marketplace and remain cost competitive if it is to have any relevance to internatioal financial systems. Page 33.

HSBC James Capel analyst Mario Traviati says market interest in Australia's oil and gas sector is set to increase as investors focus on a huge exploration effort planned for this year. Rising oil prices, exploration success and takeover activity have reativated the sector after 10 years in the doldrums which ended in 1996. Page 35.
THE AGE

With the release of the mid-year review due today, Acting Treasurer John Fahey said yesterday the Federal Government was "on target broadly", signalling that expectations for some indicators such as business investment would be strengthened. However, poor or indifferent results last week in the form of figures for the current-account deficit, job advertisements, retail trade and building approvals led to further speculation over another early interest rate reduction. Page C1.

According to the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry survey of investor confidence, business people are more dissatisfied with the economy than at any time since late 1993, with business expecting marginal improvements in business conditions, earnings growth and interest rates, but little improvement in other areas. Page C1.

In a brief statement last week, Heytesbury Holdings said the position of finance director Peter Wood had been made redundant and two new positions had been created in its place - commercial manager and group chief accountant-financial controller. Heytesbury said former Ernst & Young partner Graeme Scott had taken Wood's place on the board and Andrew Quenby would take up the role of commercial manager. Page C1.

In an effort to recover A$750,000 lost in the collapse of Perth financial advisory company, Astute Financial Group, the Australian Securities Commission has begun legal action against Personal & Business Financial Planning Pty Ltd, alleging negligence and other causes of action. Page C2.

Despite Placer Dome Inc withdrawing its offer to buy Papua New Guinea's Porgera mine after Highlands Gold failed to secure a A$160 million underwriting agreement, the Highlands board will meet today to consider alternative plans to put to Placer. Page 2.

St George Bank is expected to win final approval for its A$2.65 billion takeover bid for Advance Bank this week with an Advance shareholders' meeting scheduled for today to vote on changes to the bank's articles of association and the required reduction in capita and a final court hearing in the Supreme Court tomorrow. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
